syllabus.note: Unit-wise syllabus from MPBSE Class 12 Chemistry blueprint.

books.book_name: NCERT Chemistry Part I & Part II

chapters.name: Vilaayan (Solutions)
topics: Concentration terms: molarity (M), molality (m), normality (N), mole fraction, ppm
Raoult's law for volatile and non-volatile solute
Ideal and non-ideal solutions: positive and negative deviation with examples
Colligative properties: relative lowering of VP, elevation of BP, depression of FP, osmotic pressure
van't Hoff factor (i) for electrolytes
Osmosis, reverse osmosis, semipermeable membrane
Henry's law for gas dissolution
Azeotropic mixtures: maximum and minimum boiling

chapters.name: Vaidyut Rasayan (Electrochemistry)
topics: Galvanic cell (Daniel cell) aur electrolytic cell
EMF of cell aur standard electrode potential
Nernst equation: E = E° - (0.0592/n) log Q at 25°C
ΔG° = -nFE° and spontaneity
Conductance: specific, molar, equivalent
Kohlrausch's law and degree of dissociation
Faraday's 1st and 2nd laws of electrolysis
Batteries: lead storage, dry cell, fuel cell
Corrosion: mechanism and prevention

chapters.name: Rasayanic Bal Gatiki (Chemical Kinetics)
topics: Rate of reaction aur rate law: rate = k[A]^m [B]^n
Order of reaction vs molecularity — difference
Zero order: k = x/t, t₁/₂ = [A₀]/2k
First order: k = (2.303/t) log [A₀]/[A], t₁/₂ = 0.693/k
Arrhenius equation: k = Ae^(-Ea/RT)
Activation energy Ea: catalyst lowers it
Effect of temperature on rate
Homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis

chapters.name: d evam f-Block ke Tatva (d and f Block Elements)
topics: General electronic configuration: (n-1)d^1-10 ns^1-2
Properties: variable oxidation states, colour, paramagnetism, catalytic activity, alloy, complex formation
Why Zn, Cd, Hg are not typical transition metals
Lanthanide contraction: cause (poor shielding by f electrons) and consequences
Actinides: radioactive, 5f series
KMnO₄: preparation and oxidizing in acidic, basic, neutral medium
K₂Cr₂O₇: preparation and oxidizing properties

chapters.name: Up-Sah Sanyojak Yaugik (Coordination Compounds)
topics: Terminology: ligand, coordination number, coordination sphere, oxidation number
IUPAC nomenclature rules
Werner's theory postulates
VBT: inner orbital (dsp²,d²sp³) vs outer orbital (sp³d²) complexes
Types of isomerism: ionisation, hydrate, linkage, coordination, geometric, optical
Stability constant of complex
Applications: photography (AgBr + Na₂S₂O₃), medicine (EDTA chelation therapy)

chapters.name: Halo Alkene Halo Arene (Haloalkanes and Haloarenes)
topics: Classification: 1°, 2°, 3° haloalkanes
Methods of preparation from alkenes, alcohols, alkanes
SN1 vs SN2 mechanism, conditions, stereochemistry
Finkelstein, Swarts, Wurtz, Sandmeyer, Gattermann reactions
Haloarenes — less reactive in nucleophilic substitution
Chloroform, iodoform preparation and uses
DDT, Freon — environmental effects

chapters.name: Alkohol Phenol aur Ether
topics: Classification: 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols
Preparation from alkenes (hydration), haloalkanes, Grignard, aldehydes/ketones
Reactions: with Na, PCl₅, HX (Lucas test), oxidation, esterification
Lucas test and Victor Meyer test for identification
Phenol: preparation from cumene, diazonium salts, chlorobenzene
Phenol reactions: Kolbe, Reimer-Tiemann, bromination, FeCl₃ test
Ether: Williamson synthesis, reaction with HI

chapters.name: Aldehyde Ketone aur Carboxylic Acid
topics: Preparation: from alcohols, acid chlorides, ozonolysis, Gattermann-Koch, Rosenmund
Nucleophilic addition: HCN, NaHSO₃, Grignard, alcohol (hemiacetal/acetal)
Cannizzaro reaction (no alpha-H aldehydes)
Aldol condensation (alpha-H required)
Tests: Tollen's, Fehling's, Benedict's, iodoform
Clemmensen reduction and Wolff-Kishner reduction
Carboxylic acid preparation and reactions
HVZ reaction, acidity comparison
Fischer esterification

chapters.name: Ameen (Amines)
topics: Classification: 1°, 2°, 3° amines; IUPAC nomenclature
Preparation: from nitroalkane, Hoffmann bromamide, nitrile, haloalkane
Basic nature: comparison of amines with NH₃
Basicity order: aliphatic vs aromatic
Hinsberg test for identification
Reactions: HNO₂, acylation, Carbylamine, Mustard oil reaction
Diazonium salts: preparation and Sandmeyer/Gattermann/coupling reactions

chapters.name: Jav Anu (Biomolecules)
topics: Carbohydrates: classification, monosaccharides, disaccharides, polysaccharides
Glucose structure (open chain), reducing nature
Reducing vs non-reducing sugars
Starch vs cellulose differences
Proteins: amino acids, peptide bond, 4 structural levels
Enzymes: definition, lock and key model
Nucleic acids: DNA vs RNA differences
Vitamins: fat-soluble (A,D,E,K) and water-soluble (B,C)
Hormones: insulin, thyroxine, testosterone, cortisone

EMF of cell aur standard electrode potential

ΔG° = -nFE° and spontaneity

Lead storage battery working with diagram

In electrolytic cell: anode is positive

chapters.name: Rasayanic Bal Gatiki (Chemical Kinetics)
chapters.difficulty_reason: Standard first order kinetics — formula based
chapters.note: Guaranteed annual: First order kinetics + half life proof
important_topics: Rate of reaction aur rate law: rate = k[A]^m [B]^n
Order of reaction vs molecularity — difference
Zero order: k = x/t, t₁/₂ = [A₀]/2k
First order: k = (2.303/t) log [A₀]/[A], t₁/₂ = 0.693/k
Arrhenius equation: k = Ae^(-Ea/RT)
Activation energy Ea: catalyst lowers it
Effect of temperature on rate
Homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis
easy_topics: Order vs molecularity difference — 2 marks table
Pseudo first order example: hydrolysis of ester
important_derivations: First order rate constant: k = (2.303/t) log [A₀]/[A]
Proof: first order t₁/₂ = 0.693/k independent of initial concentration (MP 2019, 2023)
important_formulas: t₁/₂ = 0.693/k  — first order (independent of initial concentration)
most_repeated_topics: Half-life proof: t₁/₂ independent of initial concentration
key_mcq_answers: First order half life: independent of initial concentration
Rate constant unit for first order: s⁻¹
Rate constant unit for zero order: mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹

chapters.name: d evam f-Block ke Tatva (d and f Block Elements)
chapters.note: No numerical: d/f block — entirely theory, no numerical | Mostly objective: 4 objective questions out of 7 marks — 57% marks from objectives | Guaranteed annual: KMnO₄ oxidizing properties
important_topics: General electronic configuration: (n-1)d^1-10 ns^1-2
Properties: variable oxidation states, colour, paramagnetism, catalytic activity, alloy, complex formation
Why Zn, Cd, Hg are not typical transition metals
Lanthanide contraction: cause (poor shielding by f electrons) and consequences
Actinides: radioactive, 5f series
KMnO₄: preparation and oxidizing in acidic, basic, neutral medium
K₂Cr₂O₇: preparation and oxidizing properties
important_reactions: KMnO₄ acidic: 2KMnO₄+3H₂SO₄ → K₂SO₄+2MnSO₄+3H₂O+5[O]  — oxidizes FeSO₄, oxalic acid, KI
most_repeated_topics: Why Zn/Cd/Hg not typical transition metals
key_mcq_answers: Lanthanide contraction cause: poor shielding by f electrons
f-block elements called: antah sankraman tatva (inner transition)
Colour in transition compounds: due to d-d transitions
Zn, Cd, Hg: not typical transition metals (d¹⁰ in all states)
KMnO₄ tulyaanki bhar in acidic medium: 31.6
Cu⁺ is colourless: 3d¹⁰ no unpaired electron
Mn maximum oxidation state: +7 in KMnO₄

most_repeated_topics: Reactivity order: R-I > R-Br > R-Cl > R-F

chapters.name: Alkohol Phenol aur Ether
important_topics: Classification: 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols

Reactions: with Na, PCl₅, HX (Lucas test), oxidation, esterification

Phenol reactions: Kolbe, Reimer-Tiemann, bromination, FeCl₃ test

important_reactions: Lucas test: 3° + HCl/ZnCl₂ → immediate turbidity. 2° = few min. 1° = no reaction.
Victor Meyer: 1° = red, 2° = blue, 3° = no colour
Phenol from cumene: C₆H₅CH(CH₃)₂ → C₆H₅OH + CH₃COCH₃
key_mcq_answers: Ether: cannot be extinguished by water — highly inflammable

chapters.name: Aldehyde Ketone aur Carboxylic Acid
chapters.note: Guaranteed annual: Cannizzaro/Aldol reaction or Tollen's/Fehling's test | 5-mark topic: Aldehyde/ketone mechanism ya carboxylic acid reactions
important_topics: Preparation: from alcohols, acid chlorides, ozonolysis, Gattermann-Koch, Rosenmund
Nucleophilic addition: HCN, NaHSO₃, Grignard, alcohol (hemiacetal/acetal)
Cannizzaro reaction (no alpha-H aldehydes)

Clemmensen reduction and Wolff-Kishner reduction
Carboxylic acid preparation and reactions
HVZ reaction, acidity comparison

easy_topics: Tollen's test = silver mirror = aldehyde only (MCQ)
important_reactions: Tollen's: RCHO + [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺ → RCOO⁻ + Ag↓ (silver mirror). Ketones do NOT react.
Fehling's: RCHO + Cu²⁺ → RCOO⁻ + Cu₂O↓ (red). Aromatic aldehydes and ketones do NOT react.
Rosenmund: RCOCl + H₂ → RCHO (Pd/BaSO₄ poisoned catalyst)
Fischer esterification: RCOOH + R'OH ⇌ RCOOR' + H₂O (H₂SO₄)
most_repeated_topics: Tollen's vs Fehling's: which compounds give positive test
Acidity of carboxylic acids — order and explanation
Preparation of aldehyde from acyl chloride (Rosenmund)
key_mcq_answers: Tollen's test: silver mirror = aldehyde only
Fehling's solution: red ppt = aliphatic aldehyde
Iodoform test positive: CH₃CO- group (acetaldehyde, acetone)
Formic acid reduces Tollen's (behaves like aldehyde)

chapters.name: Ameen (Amines)
chapters.note: No numerical: Amines — entirely theory | Mostly objective: 4 objective + 1 very short answer = all 6 marks from easy questions
important_topics: Classification: 1°, 2°, 3° amines; IUPAC nomenclature
Preparation: from nitroalkane, Hoffmann bromamide, nitrile, haloalkane

Basicity order: aliphatic vs aromatic

Reactions: HNO₂, acylation, Carbylamine, Mustard oil reaction

easy_topics: Hinsberg: 1° soluble in KOH, 3° no reaction
important_reactions: Hoffmann: RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH → RNH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O (one C less)
Carbylamine: RNH₂ + CHCl₃ + 3KOH → RNC + 3KCl + 3H₂O (foul smell, 1° only)
Hinsberg: 1° → C₆H₅SO₂NHR (soluble KOH). 2° → C₆H₅SO₂NR₂ (insoluble). 3° → no reaction.
Sandmeyer: + CuCN → ArCN, + CuCl → ArCl, + CuBr → ArBr
most_repeated_topics: Diazonium salt reactions: Sandmeyer, Gattermann, coupling
Why ethylamine more basic than aniline (MP 2023)
key_mcq_answers: Carbylamine reaction: test for primary amine only
Hoffmann bromamide: product has one less carbon than reactant amide
Hinsberg test: 1° soluble in KOH, 2° insoluble, 3° no reaction

one_mark_question_facts.note: Q1 to Q4 mein 28 questions hote hain = 28 marks. Mostly from these patterns:

formulas: t₁/₂ = 0.693/k  — first order (independent of initial concentration)

practical_paper.not_giving_practical_consequence: 30 marks mein se zero. Overall passing affected. Dena zaroori hai.

components.name: Practical experiments written record and performance

activities_vs_experiments.experiment: Full procedure, observations, calculations, result. Example: titration, Mohr's salt.
activities_vs_experiments.activity: Shorter demonstration. Example: testing functional groups, chromatography.

paper_difficulty_analysis.note: 40% marks sirf Q1-Q4 objectives se aa jaate hain. Agar objectives achhe karo toh passing pakki. Physics se thoda easier structure.

tips: Q1 se Q4 pehle complete karo — 28 marks, relatively easy, 35-40 min mein karo
Chemical equations hamesha balance karke likho — unbalanced = marks cut
IUPAC names mein spelling dhyan se likho
Reaction mechanism mein steps clearly number karo
Tollen's test, iodoform test, carbylamine test — ye tests description ke saath likho
Unit 10 (Biomolecules) mein vitamins table ek baar achhi tarah yaad karo — 5 marks pakke
Numericals mein: Given, Formula, Substitution, Answer with units
Structural formulas banana mat bhoolna jahan maanga ho
Difference/comparison questions mein table banao — examiner ko marks dena easy hota hai
Internal choice mein woh question chuno jisme zyaada reactions/equations yaad hain
Question number aur set number cover page par zaroori likho
Rough work clearly ROUGH WORK mark karo last page pe

targets.strategy: Q1-Q4 (28 objectives) mein se 20-22 sahi karo = 20-22 marks. + 1-2 very short answer questions = 23-26 marks. Passing pakka.
focus_chapters: Unit 10 (Biomolecules) — vitamins table yaad karo, 5-7 marks easy
Unit 9 (Amines) — carbylamine test, Hinsberg test, 4 MCQ easy
Unit 4 (d/f Block) — 4 MCQ + 1 short = 7 marks, memory based
Unit 3 (Kinetics) — t₁/₂ formula, order vs molecularity
Unit 7 (Alcohols) — Lucas test, Kolbe reaction, Phenol FeCl₃ test

targets.strategy: Objectives (22-24) + 3-4 very short answer + 2 laghu questions = ~40 marks
Full objectives (28) + very short answer (12-14) + laghu (6-9) + 1 long answer = 55-65 marks
targets.tip: Units 2, 3, 8 ke derivations aur mechanisms prepare karo for full marks.

easy_chapters_to_complete_first: Unit 4 (d/f Block) — memory based facts, 7 marks

internal_assessment.note: No separate internal assessment — 30 marks practical covers non-theory component

answer_sheet_rules: question_number_note: Haan — har answer ke upar question number likhna zaroori hai. Examiner dhundhta hai. Nahi likha toh marks confusion ho sakta hai.
set_number_note: Haan — apna set number (A/B/C/D) answer sheet ke cover page par compulsory likhna hota hai.
question_copy_note: Answer sheet mein poora question likhna zaroori nahi. Sirf question number likho aur answer shuru karo.
rough_work: Answer sheet ka last page rough work ke liye. Clearly ROUGH WORK likho. Rough work pe marks nahi milte lekin kaam aata hai.
supplementary_sheet: Supplementary sheet lene se marks nahi katenge. Zaroorat ho toh lo. Lekin unnecessary blank pages waste mat karo.
sequence_note: Questions ka sequence follow karna zaroori nahi. Jo aata ho pehle karo. Lekin question number clearly likho.
last_to_first: Haan — paper last se bhi start kar sakte ho. Koi rule nahi ki sequence follow karo.
long_answer_position: Long answers hamesha paper ke last mein nahi hote. Section D aur E mein hote hain lekin sequence alag ho sakti hai.
section_name_before_section: Section ka naam likhna compulsory nahi lekin recommended hai. Examiner ko navigate karna easy hota hai.
line_after_each_question: Zaroori nahi. Lekin do lines draw karne se answer clearly separate dikhta hai — good practice.
cutting_overwriting: Cuts se marks directly nahi katenge. Ek clean line se kato. Clean cutting acceptable hai.
short_before_long: Pehle short answers attempt karo phir long — marks nahi katenge. Jo bhi order suit kare.
sub_questions: Sub questions matlab ek question ke andar (a), (b), (c) parts hote hain. Har part ke marks alag alag hote hain.

pen_rules.note: Blue pen se main answer, black se headings/underline. Ya sirf ek color bhi chalega.

exam_writing_rules.rough_work_rules: Answer sheet ka last page rough work ke liye. Clearly ROUGH WORK likho. Rough work pe marks nahi milte lekin kaam aata hai.
exam_writing_rules.overwriting_rules: Cuts se marks directly nahi katenge. Ek clean line se kato. Clean cutting acceptable hai.
exam_writing_rules.cutting_rules: Cuts se marks directly nahi katenge. Ek clean line se kato. Clean cutting acceptable hai.
